name: The Axiom Skin Launch — Chicago Hub, 2198
creator: Axiom Corponation / Axiom BioInterface Division
description: On September 3, 2198, Axiom unveiled SkinNet — a subdermal neural mesh that replaced discrete BCI hardware with a full-body conductive lattice, marketed as 'wearing the network.' The launch event in the Chicago Hub's Crown Atrium featured live demonstrations where volunteers experienced shared sensory states simultaneously, and the product sold out its first 200,000 units in eleven minutes. Within six months, SkinNet had become the defining aspirational technology of Tier 3 and the status symbol of Tier 4.
medium: live event, neural feed simulcast, holographic projection
cultural_impact: SkinNet fundamentally altered the social landscape of neural connectivity, creating a two-tier BCI experience and spawning both the Resonance collective music scene and the Flatskin rejection movement as direct cultural responses.
controversy: Long-term SkinNet users began reporting 'boundary dissolution' — difficulty distinguishing their own sensory input from network bleed — by 2203. Axiom's internal research on this effect, leaked in 2206, suggested the company knew before launch.
story_hooks: The volunteer demonstrators from the launch event were never part of any public follow-up study — locating them reveals a pattern of neurological decline.
The original SkinNet prototype, capable of involuntary sensory override, was quietly shelved; a working unit exists somewhere.
A character's boundary dissolution episodes are revealing someone else's memories — someone who died.
